findings.current: That’s what I’m saying—what are they rescuing? If they’re rescuing a corpse, that isn’t a rescue. It’s cleanup.
findings.defect: “Cleanup” is broader and more dismissive than 수습, which specifically contrasts rescuing a living person with recovering a corpse.
findings.rationale: The source hinges on the distinction between 구조, rescue, and 수습, recovery of the dead.
findings.replacement: That’s what I’m saying—what are they rescuing? You don’t rescue a corpse. You recover it.
findings.source: 아니 그러니까 뭘 구조하냐고. 시체 구조하면 그게 구조냐, 수습이지.

findings.current: Like someone’s sharp rebuke, the situation was more serious than expected.
findings.defect: The comparison is attached to the situation itself, producing an illogical image instead of attributing the observation to the preceding commenter.
findings.rationale: 누군가의 일침처럼 refers back to the pointed chat remark that exposed the gravity of the situation.
findings.replacement: As one commenter had bluntly pointed out, the situation was more serious than expected.

findings.current: Then why hasn’t anyone come out? They said the Battle Map Gate is close enough to touch with your nose if you fell flat on your face.
findings.defect: The draft misparses 전투지도 as a proper name, “Battle Map Gate.” The source says the battle site is extremely close to the Gate.
findings.rationale: 전투지 is the battle site, while 도 is the topic particle; the sentence describes the distance between that site and the Gate.
findings.replacement: Then why hasn’t anyone come out? They said the battle site was just a stone’s throw from the Gate.
findings.source: 근데 왜 아무도 안 와. 전투지도 게이트에서 엎어지면 코 닿을 거리라며.

findings.current: They were carrying stretchers covered with large sheets. As the stretchers swayed with each step, one blood-soaked hand slipped out from beneath the cloth.
findings.defect: The draft changes the single stretcher and single covering cloth into multiple stretchers and sheets.
findings.rationale: Both 들것 and 천 are singular in the source, and the later hand belongs to the person on that one stretcher.
findings.replacement: They were carrying a stretcher covered with a large sheet. As it swayed with each step, one blood-soaked hand slipped out from beneath the cloth.
findings.source: 그들의 손에는 커다란 천에 덮인 들것이 들려 있었다. 걸음에 들것이 흔들리자 피에 젖은 손 하나가 천 밖으로 툭 밀려 나왔다.

findings.current: “Whoa. Why are there so many of these?”
findings.defect: “Whoa” expresses general surprise but omits the explicit cue that the sight startled Taekyung.
findings.rationale: 깜짝이야 specifically says that he was startled, preserving his immediate reaction on emerging from the Gate.
findings.replacement: “That startled me. Why are there so many of these?”

findings.defect: 뚱이 is Patrick Star’s Korean name here, not a generic claim that the speaker is fat, so the draft loses the recognizable deadpan joke.
findings.rationale: The line invokes the established Korean rendering of the SpongeBob meme, whose English punchline is “No, this is Patrick.”

findings.defect: The draft adds subjective uncertainty and weakens Taekyung’s bald, deadpan denial after breaking the lock.
findings.rationale: 열려 있던데 directly asserts that it was open; it does not mean that it merely appeared open.

findings.defect: The draft translates the individual characters of the fixed expression 전광석화, producing a nonexistent petrification command and obscuring the speed joke.
findings.rationale: 전광석화 means moving in a flash and is also the Korean name of Pokémon’s Quick Attack, matching “Warlordmon” and the rapid shaking that immediately follows.

findings.current: “Why on earth did you even bring that thing here…?”
findings.defect: The draft omits 잡아, which explicitly says Taekyung captured the Skeleton Warlord before bringing it back.
findings.rationale: 잡아 오다 combines catching or capturing something with bringing it back; the capture is a stated action, not merely implied transport.
findings.replacement: “Why on earth did you capture that thing and bring it back…?”

summary: The draft contains two scene-fact errors involving the battle site and the number of stretchers, plus several mistranslated jokes, omitted action details, and localized register issues.
